title: Localized evaluation precomposition
statement:
theorem tensorHomEvaluation_precomposition (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (L L' M : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (b : DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj L') :
    letI := schemeDerivedTensorMonoidal X
    let E := fun L M : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ ↦
      ((schemeDerivedInternalHomResolutionIso X L M).hom ⊗ₘ
          𝟙 (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L)) ≫
        pullbackTensorModelMap X (homComplex (R := X.sheaf) L
          ((schemeHomKInjectiveResolution X).obj M)) L ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (schemeTensorHomUncurry X _ L M (𝟙 _)) ≫
        schemeHomResolutionInverse X M
    ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) X.sheaf).map
        (b.hom.op, 𝟙 (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)) ⊗ₘ 𝟙 (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L)) ≫ E L M =
      (𝟙 _ ⊗ₘ b.hom) ≫ E L' M

source.place: Tag 08DJ; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0A90 and 0A96; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08DJ, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A90, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A96 (read online)

proof.text: For a chain map b:L -> Lprime, put H=Hom(L,I(M)), Hprime=Hom(Lprime,I(M)), and f=Hom(b,I(identity M)). Apply the localized evaluation theorem first with identity source map and b in the tensor variable, then with f in the source variable and identity tensor map. Simplify identities and equate the common localized uncurrying. This gives (Qf tensor identity QL);U_L = (identity QHprime tensor Qb);U_Lprime, where U is the raw localized evaluation followed by the inverse augmentation.

Naturality of Localization.fac for (b.op, identity M), together with Q.map_id, gives RHom(Qb,identity);j_L = j_Lprime;Qf for the exact fixed resolution isomorphisms in the statement. Tensor this equality with identity QL and compose with raw evaluation. The previous raw square and tensor interchange give the normalized dinaturality square for Qb. This is evaluation_chain; normalized_chain proves the tensor algebra in an abstract monoidal category.

Use DerivedCategory.right_fac, the cochain specialization of right-fraction representation, to write the given derived b.hom as inv(Qs);Qg with s:R -> L and g:R -> Lprime and IsIso(Qs). Apply the chain square to s and g. Dinaturality for an invertible s implies dinaturality for its inverse: precompose by RHom(s,identity) tensor identity, use the functor law to cancel RHom(s) followed by RHom(inv s), commute the two tensor variables, use the square for s, and cancel inv s followed by s. Dinaturality is stable under composition by the contravariant functor map_comp law and tensor interchange. Combine these two proved generic lemmas to obtain the stated square for inv(Qs);Qg. All witnesses are local in a proof; no data are defined from an unproved existence theorem. No K-flatness, boundedness, or additional chain homotopy argument is used.

proof_origin.place: Tags 08DJ and 0A90; localized chain evaluation followed by Localization.fac naturality and DerivedCategory.right_fac. Generic inversion and composition of dinaturality squares are proved in Lean.
